page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with the PassMark CPU score and extended instructions test placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contribute to strong multi-threaded performance, as seen in bzip3 decompression and Geekbench compiling tests. Static web serving throughput is also highly efficient, reaching the top 10% tier. However, single-core performance and uncached large-block memory write bandwidth remain in the average range, and the PassMark memory score is positioned in the lower 25%.

Given its high core count and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D96s_v6 is qualitatively cost-efficient for dense, multi-threaded workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 flags makes it highly capable for CPU-based machine learning inference, as demonstrated by strong prompt processing speeds on medium and large LLM models. It is well-suited for enterprise-grade web serving, database operations, software compilation, and parallelized data processing tasks.
